CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left shoulder pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mrs. Anderson is a 44-year-old female presenting with left shoulder pain that has lasted for one week. She reports the pain started during a gymnastics class when she may have toppled over into a weird position during a certain move. She states she went overboard with the movement. Any kind of movement on her left shoulder causes pain. She tried taking Tylenol for two or three days without relief. On physical examination, movement in multiple directions causes pain. X-ray shows no broken bone or fracture. Assessment is that she has hurt her joint. She was advised to use ibuprofen 600 mg three times a day for one week. If still painful, she can use ice or heat pad. She is instructed to rest her left arm while healing and to avoid carrying heavy weights, using her right hand instead for the next three to four weeks. She should return for follow-up if pain persists after three weeks.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Prior surgery on left arm.

MEDICATIONS
Tylenol (used for two to three days, not effective).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Participates in gymnastics class.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Left shoulder: pain with movement in multiple directions. X-ray of left shoulder: no fracture or broken bone noted.

RESULTS
X-ray of left shoulder: no fracture or broken bone.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Left shoulder joint injury. Plan: Ibuprofen 600 mg three times daily for one week. Alternative options include Advil or Aleve. Ice or heat pad as needed for pain relief. Rest left arm for three to four weeks, avoiding heavy weights and using right hand instead. Follow-up in three weeks if pain persists; may obtain repeat x-ray at that time depending on clinical status.
